scientific_question: Before endpoint collapse, are Original-DRTP checkpoints more sensitive than good Original-DRTP and matched UTR checkpoints to future rollout/update randomness?

minibatch_negative_control.structural_note: The frozen 4x64 rollout and minibatch_graphs=256 produce one full-rollout minibatch per PPO epoch, so permutation-only effects should be numerically negligible.

primary_sensitivity_metrics: median pairwise cosine distance of cumulative actor parameter deltas
median pairwise policy-output JS divergence on the frozen probe bank
mechanism_pass_all_required: at least two adverse or catastrophic DRTP source seeds in at least two cohorts show the same sensitivity signature
the signature is present by update horizon 16 and precedes branch-level endpoint degradation at horizon 64
each replicated adverse DRTP checkpoint exceeds its matched UTR checkpoint on at least two primary sensitivity metrics
the adverse DRTP checkpoint ranks in the top two of five within its cohort on the same metrics while its matched UTR does not
the held-out B5 cohort reproduces the discovery signature without redefining thresholds
the formal-positive 2300 control cohort and high-return seeds do not exhibit an equally strong complete signature
the conclusion is unchanged when each one branch is removed in turn
forbidden: merging RNG branches as independent n
